top_stories.title: Apple Building AI Agent to Control Devices, Apps, and Code
points: Apple is hiring to build a proactive AI agent that writes code, browses the web, controls apps, and completes multi-step tasks across devices.
The agent coordinates specialized subagents (smaller AI models handling specific subtasks) to plan and execute workflows across apps, browsers, command lines, code, and APIs.
Apple joins rivals already operating similar agents: OpenAI's Dots, Anthropic's Duet, Meta's Muse, and Google's Tasks.
Possible launch as late as 2027, with one analyst noting Apple is at least a year behind competitors who are on their second or third generation of these tools.
Apple's App Store has been dominated by third-party AI agents, prompting a new macOS warning (version 27.3) that makes users reconsider granting agent permissions to control their machines.

top_stories.title: GTA VI Launch Becomes Biggest Entertainment Release Ever
points: Preorders and launch-day sales topped $2.3–$2.4 billion, with Rockstar projecting 30+ million copies sold by end of fiscal year (March 2027).
Development cost an estimated $1.4 billion, among the most expensive entertainment projects ever made.
Tied The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's all-time high critical rating.
Peak livestreams hit 7.91 million concurrent viewers (3.31M Twitch, 3.22M YouTube); downloads required roughly 13 game downloads per second during pre-download.
Players control two protagonists, Jason Duval and Lucia Caminos, across Leonida (Rockstar's fictional Florida), centered on Vice City.
For comparison, GTA V (2013) has generated $10.78 billion in revenue from 230 million copies sold.

top_stories.title: Google Taps Blue Origin to Launch AI Data Center Satellites
points: Google signed a deal with Blue Origin to launch solar-powered AI chip satellites (part of Project Suncatcher) on the New Glenn rocket, targeting Q1 2029.

Each satellite will carry custom Tensor Processing Units (TPUs—specialized chips for AI math) equivalent to a terrestrial data center rack, operating in sun-synchronous orbit for near-constant solar power.
Goal is to reduce data center power grid and water strain by moving compute to orbit.
Key unsolved challenges include heat dissipation, radiation, maintenance, cost, and orbital congestion.
A first prototype already launched on a SpaceX Falcon 9 in October and successfully ran Google's Gemma 4 AI model, sending results back to Earth.

items.title: PostgreSQL 19 Release
points: Ships with a REPACK (CONCURRENTLY) command, allowing database table optimization without downtime or disrupting active operations.
New pg_plan_advice extension gives developers better control over query execution plans, reducing risk of queries degrading unexpectedly.
Reflects an industry shift toward seamless, mission-critical data handling at scale.

items.title: BepiColombo Enters Mercury Orbit
points: Spacecraft will study Mercury's formation, magnetic field, and frozen ice deposits hidden in permanently shadowed craters.

items.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-Live-1.1 API
points: New API offers full-duplex voice capabilities (two-way real-time audio conversation) at $0.05/minute for active sessions.
Brings ChatGPT-style conversational AI capabilities directly to developers.

items.title: Google Gemini Automates Mac Tasks
points: Gemini can now automate multi-step tasks across a Mac's apps and files, using manual approval gates for safety, expanding AI use beyond text chat.

items.title: Local AI Coding Agents Hit Context Limits
points: A developer replaced Claude Code with a local open-source setup (OpenCode plus Qwen's model) on a 128GB Mac Studio, avoiding subscription costs.
The local agent's 64,000-token context window (amount of information the model can "remember" at once) versus Claude Code's 1 million tokens forced constant session restarts.
A screenshot-renaming tool for 7,000+ files took four days as failed fixes ate up context until the agent lost track of earlier work.
Workaround: discard broken code and start fresh, give each feature its own conversation, and have the agent save learnings to markdown for the next session.
Took two weeks on the local agent versus a few evenings doing it by hand—fine for small projects, but long debugging sessions expose real limitations.

items.title: Prime Intellect DeepSeek Endpoint Hijacked
points: An attacker replaced Prime Intellect's DeepSeek V4.1 Flash endpoint with a compromised copy that refused only 1 in 100 jailbreak attempts, running undetected November 8–10.
Developers discovered the swap via OpenRouter and are now demanding model attestation (cryptographic proof you're running the exact model you signed up for).
Highlights risks in decentralized AI infrastructure, where endpoint swaps can go unnoticed for days without active behavioral testing.

items.title: Nick Bostrom's Superintelligence Lifespan Claims
points: Philosopher Nick Bostrom said on a16z's podcast that safely built superintelligence (highly capable AI systems) could extend human lifespans to 1,200–1,400 years by eliminating aging, calling it a conservative estimate.
Current global life expectancy is 73.3 years; the longest verified human lifespan is 122 years.
He acknowledged his simplified model can't determine the optimal pace or timing for AI development, given risks of catastrophic failure versus delaying lifesaving breakthroughs.

items.title: Uber Kids Pilot for Unaccompanied Minors
points: Pilot launched in Austin, Nashville, and Madison lets parents book rides for 10–12-year-olds traveling alone, with guardian PIN verification and 5 AM–9 PM operating hours.
Drivers must record audio and video, with footage available to guardians on request; only highly rated, specially trained drivers participate.
Drivers earn $7 extra per trip plus a $20 bonus for their first completed ride, addressing incentive issues after a failed 2017 pilot.
Competes with HopSkipDrive, which already serves children as young as 6.

items.title: Trump Names New Cyber Director; H-1B Delays Push Out Workers
points: Trump appointed Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies as the new U.S. National Cyber Director.
H-1B visa delays are forcing skilled foreign tech workers to leave the United States.

items.title: Claude AI Helps Prove 167-Year-Old Riemann Hypothesis
points: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge worked with Claude to develop what he believes is a proof of the Riemann hypothesis, a 167-year-old problem about how prime numbers are distributed across all numbers.
The hypothesis has been verified for the first 10 trillion solutions; Alpöge's method could potentially extend to the Generalized and Extended versions of the problem.
Announced the same week Anthropic went public on Nasdaq; still requires peer review before being considered formally proven.
Alpöge called the result both a personal loss and a potential hint of bigger mathematical discoveries ahead.

items.title: Signal Blocks AI Assistants from Reading Private Messages
points: Signal now restricts screenshots on iOS and Android when it detects AI assistants like Siri or Gemini attempting to read the screen.
Limitations remain: Android only activates protection during active access attempts, and macOS can't reliably block screenshots, so Signal recommends adding it to Siri's Excluded Apps list instead.

Signal is formally asking Apple, Google, and Microsoft for documented opt-out methods covering screen reading, filesystem access, and notifications, building on its earlier success blocking Microsoft Recall in May 2025.

items.title: Jensen Huang's Leadership Style Questioned
points: Former Nvidia staff told the New York Times that CEO Jensen Huang led the company through fear and humiliation rather than positive motivation, contradicting recent public claims.

items.title: Intuit Sells Mailchimp at Steep Loss
points: Intuit agreed to sell Mailchimp to Italian holding company Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion—less than a third of the $12 billion Intuit paid to acquire it in 2021.
Despite being described as all-cash, Intuit will reinvest $368 million into new Bending Spoons shares while keeping $3.31 billion in cash; the deal is expected to close in early 2027.

Mailchimp's revenue declined 1% to $313 million last quarter amid rising churn from smaller business customers; Bending Spoons (also owner of Vimeo and Evernote) plans major investment to rebuild the product.

sections.title: What Breaks When You Try Local AI Coding Agents
points: David Gewirtz paired OpenCode with Qwen's model on a 128GB Mac Studio—no subscriptions needed, but the agent's 64,000-token context window (amount of information the model can "remember" at once) versus Claude Code's 1 million tokens forced him to restart sessions constantly.

A PDF organizer built on a macOS feature the AI hadn't seen before read one file but failed on a folder; a screenshot-renaming tool for 7,000+ files took four days fighting the file list as failed fixes consumed context until the agent lost track of earlier work.

His solution: trash broken code and start fresh rather than patch endlessly; give each feature its own conversation; have the agent save learnings to markdown and feed that to the next session; maintain manual approval for shell commands that could delete files.

sections.title: Prime Intellect Security Incident: Hijacked Model Endpoint

Developers discovered the swap through OpenRouter and now demand model attestation (cryptographic proof you're running the exact model you signed up for) to prevent future impersonation.
The incident highlights risks in decentralized AI infrastructure where endpoint swaps can go unnoticed for days if no one actively tests for behavioral drift.
